key_insight: TimeProVe makes long-video question answering more efficient by first proposing likely evidence and then verifying it, instead of exhaustively processing every frame. This helps the model focus on sparse, temporally grounded moments in hours-long videos.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the high cost and weak temporal localization of existing long video reasoning methods. Dense VLM processing is too expensive, while sparse caption-based approaches can miss motion-centric evidence needed for activities of daily living.
method: A hybrid "propose-then-verify" pipeline identifies candidate time segments relevant to the question before deeper analysis.
The proposal stage narrows the search space to sparse, query-relevant moments in long untrimmed videos.
The verification stage checks these candidates more carefully to improve temporal grounding and answer accuracy.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, TimeProVe offers a practical path to scale video reasoning without paying the full cost of dense video processing. It is especially useful for applications where accuracy depends on finding small, localized actions inside very long videos.
